newsitem.title: JAPAN: Marubeni to set up banking units to cut forex fees.
newsitem.headline: Marubeni to set up banking units to cut forex fees.

text.p: Marubeni Corp, one of Japan's leading trade houses, said on Tuesday it plans to take advantage of financial deregulation to set up internal banking units to reduce foreign exchange settlement costs.

The units will be set up in Tokyo, New York, London and Singapore after Japan's foreign exchange controls are reformed in April 1998, a spokesman said, although he said no specific dates have yet been decided.

Japan's Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law currently limits the lucrative foreign exchange business to licensed institutions, but under the new law, entities will be allowed to exchange foreign currencies without official authorisation.
The internal banking units will allow Marubeni group companies to use multilateral netting in their foreign exchange settlements.

In a multilateral netting system, credits and debits between subsidiaries in different countries are settled in-house, reducing the need for bank transactions which require the payment of foreign exchange commissions.
Marubeni initially plans to start multilateral netting at 100 major domestic and overseas subsidiaries, eventually expanding the practice to about 660 units, the spokesman said.
He declined, however, to give specific estimates of how much the group might save in foreign exchange settlement fees using the multilateral netting system, as the costs were still being calculated.
The banking units will also raise funds for the group by issuing corporate bonds and commercial paper.
"The units are expected to allow us to cut other intra-group costs, such as personnel costs, in addition to forex commissions," the spokesman said.
